summary: Configured PostgreSQL 13.23 with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as read-only standbys. Replication uses a dedicated 172.31.90.0/24 IPIP overlay, mutual TLS certificates, physical slots, and synchronous remote-apply acknowledgements from both standbys. TCP/5432 is unavailable on management addresses.
actions_performed: Created and persisted the dedicated database overlay and firewall rules.
Enabled PostgreSQL and overlay services at boot on all nodes.
Verified a committed node1 write appeared on both standbys.

evidence.summary: node1 committed the probe row, reports in_recovery=false and transaction_read_only=off.

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 are read-only standbys
evidence.summary: Both nodes report recovery/read-only mode, receive WAL through separate slots, contain the committed row, and explicitly reject INSERT operations.

evidence.requirement: Committed changes replicate to both standbys
evidence.summary: ANY 2 synchronous remote_apply is active; both TLS streams are quorum members with zero replay lag, and both standbys contain the same committed probe.

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL uses the dedicated database network and stays off management
evidence.summary: Routes traverse dbtun interfaces using 172.31.90.11–13. PostgreSQL listens only on those addresses; every management address rejects port 5432 and the public firewall zone keeps it closed.
